Subject: Follow-up: VPC connectivity + integration questions

Hi Lauren / Marissa / Jonas,

Thanks for the call earlier — that was helpful. A few follow-ups from our infra and security teams so we can scope the PoC: 

1) Connectivity model: We need clarification on options for private connectivity. Do you support AWS VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink), or do you require a dedicated VPN / peering? What are tradeoffs around egress and regional routing?

2) IP allowlist: Our security team prefers IP allowlisting for outbound requests from our VPC to Redwood. Can you provide the current IP ranges, and is there a CIDR-sized list we can put into our firewall?

3) DNS & Egress: We use internal DNS; will DNS resolution to Redwood endpoints work over a PrivateLink connection? Any special DNS forwarding required? Also, what domains/ports need to be open for egress?

4) mTLS / Auth: For highly regulated data, we prefer mTLS between services. Do you support mutual TLS for API calls, or is it API-key only? If mTLS is supported, what certificate provisioning workflow do you expect?

5) SDK / routing: We're planning to use Redwood SDK for embeddings + reranker + generation. Are there recommended client-side routing patterns to direct embeddings to dedicated pools vs generation? Any headers or routing keys we should set?

If you can send a short architecture diagram and an IP allowlist template, that would be great. Can we aim to kick off a short PoC next week (Feb 17-20)?

Thanks,
Sanjay

Hi Sanjay — great questions, thanks for laying these out. Summary and proposed next steps below from our discovery: 

Quick answers (high level):
- Connectivity: We support multiple models: AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoints) for private, no-internet egress in-region; customer VPN/peering is supported for on-premises networks; Dedicated (reserved) capacity is an alternative for higher throughput with isolated GPU pools.
- IP allowlist: We can provide stable egress IP ranges for public endpoints and a smaller set for dedicated hosts; for PrivateLink, egress is internal so IP allowlist requirements are minimal but you may need to allow the VPC endpoint ENIs.
- DNS & egress: For PrivateLink we provide an internal DNS name to resolve to the endpoint. If you use our Public API over the Internet, you'll need standard DNS/egress rules (HTTPS 443) to our domains.
- mTLS/Auth: We offer API-key + OAuth for standard integrations. mTLS is supported for Private deployments and Dedicated in some configurations — we'll need to align on cert provisioning (you can bring certs via your PKI or we can provision short-lived certs via a CSR flow).
- SDK/routing: SDK supports explicit route headers (x-redwood-cluster, x-redwood-mode) to choose generation vs embeddings pools and to pin model variants. For embeddings + rerankers we usually recommend sending embeddings to a dedicated embedding pool (lower-precision quantized variant) and routing generation to the latest verified variant.

Attachments I will follow up with: architecture diagram + an IP allowlist template. Proposed next steps:
1) Jonas to share an architecture diagram covering PrivateLink + DNS notes and sample firewall rules.
2) We'll provide IP ranges and a sample allowlist CSV.
3) Align on auth: short call between your security and our infra (Jonas) to decide between mTLS vs API key for the PoC.
4) Schedule PoC kickoff (Feb 17-20) — please confirm availability.

I’ll attach a lightweight PoC checklist and our standard connectivity diagram in a follow-up.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop

Subject: Re: Follow-up: VPC connectivity + integration questions

Hi all — attaching an architecture sketch and an IP allowlist template to make this concrete. Key implementation notes below: 

- PrivateLink (AWS VPC endpoints): We publish private hosted zone names you can resolve in your VPC (e.g., api.internal.redwood.com -> endpoint ENI IPs). No public internet egress required for PrivateLink traffic. You will need to create an Interface VPC Endpoint in the same region and enable DNS integration so the private hosted zone overrides public DNS.

- IP allowlist: For customers using public endpoint egress, we provide a set of egress IPs per region (see attached CSV). For PrivateLink, instead of IP ranges you should allow traffic to the endpoint's ENIs and your NAT/route rules.

- DNS: Enable resolver rules forwarding for cross-account/private hosted zone resolution if your VPC is in a shared services account. If you use split-horizon DNS, ensure your internal resolver forwards queries to the VPC resolver.

- mTLS: For Private & Dedicated deployments we support mTLS. Typical flow: 1) customer generates CSR -> 2) we sign/issue a cert with short TTL (or you upload your cert) -> 3) we include expected CN/SAN in allowed peer list. For PoC, API-key over PrivateLink is usually fastest; mTLS is recommended for production with regulated data.

- SDK routing: Set header x-redwood-cluster: embeddings-prod for embedding calls and x-redwood-cluster: gen-latency-1 for generation. For reranking pipelines, send candidate embeddings to the embedding pool and call the reranker on generation pool with the provided rerank endpoint. We'll share sample code snippets once you confirm PoC targets (embeddings dim, model versions).

Attachments: redwood-vpc-arch-diagram.png (network diagram), finpay-ip-allowlist-template.csv (IP ranges + region mapping).

— Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
